lines.t: Khesh-Ura rises from the red dunes like a bowl of green water set on a table of rust. Palms ring a deep oasis, and every roof is tiled in the colour of old brass.
Lizardfolk drovers lead long-necked beasts through the gate, tongues flicking at the air. The air itself is dry enough to crackle, and the sun overhead is a pale coin.
In the plaza, a stone pillar the colour of dawn stands beside the fountain. The mark in your palm gives a small, pleased pulse.
The sluice chamber is dim and wet, and it stinks of rotting weed. A great iron wheel has been jammed with a felled pillar, and the river beyond it is only a thin trickle.
Something green and heavy sits on the wheel, chewing. It has a tax collector's chain around its neck, and a sack of coins in its lap that it is using as a pillow.
Queen's water. Queen's rules. Little shiny one want to drink, little shiny one pay.
The city is thirsty. Move the pillar.
The Troll Brute slumps against the wheel and does not get up. The weed on its shoulders curls and goes grey.
You put your shoulder to the felled pillar, and with a groan of old iron it rolls aside. Behind it, water begins to roar.
In the troll's sack, among the coins, is a little glass seal stamped with a crown and a sun, and a single line of writing: By order of Her Brilliance Ismerel, who holds the Zenith.
Another shard. And a queen who already has it.
The Boar Hollow is a bowl of baked clay, littered with old bones and the splintered shafts of spears. Wallows ring the walls, each one churned deep.
At the far end, half-lit by a shaft of sun, stands a boar the size of a wagon. One tusk is snapped. The other is curved like a scimitar and stained rust-red at the root.
It lifts its head and looks at you with eyes the colour of old amber. It has been waiting for hunters for a very long time.
Sandtusk goes down on its knees, and then on its side, with a sound like a falling wall. The dust takes a long time to settle.
The great curved tusk has come loose where you struck it. It is rust-red at the root, as the stories said, and heavier than it looks.
It was only protecting its hollow. I wonder who taught it to hate hunters.
You take the tusk as proof. Kiss'a will want to see it.
